title: Linux - SUSE Session and Disk-Service Escalation Indicators
html:
SUSE Session and Disk-Service Escalation Indicators

SSH session authorization through PAM

CVE-2025-6018 affected SUSE 15 PAM configurations in which an SSH authentication stack loaded pam_env before the session stack loaded pam_systemd. When pam_env read a user's .pam_environment, that user could supply XDG_SEAT and XDG_VTNR values that made an SSH session appear physically active to Polkit. An allow_active=yes action could then become available to a remote user. This changes session authorization; it does not by itself guarantee root access. SUSE fixed the default user-environment behavior in pam and the module placement generated by pam-config.[1][2]

Inspect the effective /etc/pam.d/sshd include chain, the order of pam_env.so and pam_systemd.so, and any explicit user_readenv=1 option. A patched pam package changes the default, but an explicit option can still request user-environment reading. A newer pam-config package does not prove that a locally modified or stale PAM stack was regenerated. Check the vendor package release and the actual configuration together.[1][2]

Active-user disk-service path

CVE-2025-6019 was an escalation path in libblockdev used through udisks2: during an XFS resize, an attacker-supplied filesystem could temporarily be mounted without the expected nosuid restriction. The route needs a usable UDisks D-Bus service, XFS resize support, a relevant Polkit action available to the caller, and an affected library package. CVE-2025-6018 is one way to gain an active-user session, but an already active user can reach the disk-service path independently.[3]

For a passive review, check the UDisks service metadata, org.freedesktop.udisks2.modify-device policy, xfs_growfs, and the installed libbd_fs2 package. SUSE lists libbd_fs2 version 2.26-150400.3.5.1 as fixed for openSUSE Leap 15.6; the exact fixed release depends on the product. Policy and package presence alone are leads, not proof that a caller can mount or resize a device. Avoid changing mounts or invoking D-Bus methods during enumeration.[3]

  • [3] SUSE CVE-2025-6019 advisory
